instruction.text: Select the plants that reproduce asexually by producing tubers.

text: Both potato and yam plants produce tubers. The tuber is the part of these plants that we harvest and eat.

hint.text: Some plants have tubers, which are thick stems that grow underground and store food for the plant. Tubers become new plants the following year.
hint.label: Tubers

instruction.text: Select the plants that reproduce asexually by producing bulbs.

text: Both onion and tulip plants produce bulbs. The bulb is the part of the onion plant that we harvest and eat.

hint.text: Some plants have bulbs, which are another type of underground food storage organ. Bulbs are typically planted in autumn and are ready to grow in spring.
hint.label: Bulbs

instruction.text: Select the plants that reproduce asexually by producing runners.

text: Both strawberry and mint plants produce runners. A runner is a stem that grows horizontally above the ground. New strawberry plants grow from the runners, while still being attached to the parent plant.

hint.text: Some plants have runners. Runners are long, horizontal stems, from which new plants can grow.
hint.label: Runners
